Fixture: 108_orientation_antitranspose_rgba_600x520.jxl
600x520 RGBA, lossless modular, metadata.orientation = 7 (anti-transpose)

Purpose
-------
The MULTI-GROUP rung AGENTS.md section 6 requires of any path that can see
more than one group. At group_dim 256 a 600x520 frame is a 3x3 grid, so the
image is assembled from nine group sub-bitstreams and only then turned.

Anti-transpose moves every sample the furthest of the eight rows -- the stored
sample at (x, y) lands at displayed (H-1-y, W-1-x) -- so a decoder that applied
the turn per group, or applied it before assembly, produces a visibly scrambled
image rather than a near miss. Displayed size is 520x600.

This is also the row `sunset_logo` uses, at a sixth of the pixel count and
without that case's cropped frames, so a failure here separates "orientation is
wrong" from "cropping is wrong".

Grading (18181-3 4.2)
---------------------
Grading is against a reference DECODE of this stream (the committed .npy, or a
fresh djxl decode), never against the original source PNG -- Part 3 bounds
decoder-vs-reference error, not encoder loss against the pre-encode image.
djxl applies the orientation itself, so the reference .npy is already in
DISPLAYED orientation and its shape is the swapped one for Table D.4's four
transposing rows. That shape agreement is the first thing the test asserts:
18181-3 4.2 condition 1 fails outright for a decoder that ignored the field.

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording
them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 7
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-orientation-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_orient_rgba_600x520_o7.png  (699883 bytes)
                sha256 9be1245a7df4628356b0156a05246cb4a5ed53f27f31c2140051632f8e5ab7ab
                Synthetic PNG, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-orientation-fixtures.sh with nothing but the standard
                library -- no third-party image was used, converted or
                consulted, and no image library is involved. PNG rather than PNM
                because PNM carries neither an alpha channel nor a metadata
                chunk, and this recipe needs both.
                The PNG carries an `eXIf` chunk holding a minimal
                little-endian TIFF header with one IFD entry, tag 0x0112
                (Orientation). cjxl has no orientation flag; this chunk is how
                the value reaches the image header, and the generating script
                verifies with jxlinfo that it arrived.

  Fixture:      16910 bytes
                sha256 87e66f792cae642ba06c34d05b2d34eb08b52be7601557d776da23afd52a0bcf

  Reference decode (djxl --output_format npy):
    108_orientation_antitranspose_rgba_600x520.npy  (4992080 bytes)
    sha256 706b03f9eec5cc7de55b8017fdae49dda09fa6e8814d4fd997b9fd7503f6ae98
    NOT committed (>= 100 KB); the test regenerates it with the pinned djxl
    and SKIPS when no djxl is available.
    Shape (1, 600, 520, 4) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2. The channel count
    includes the alpha channel: djxl interleaves the extra channels after the
    colour ones, which is the same order G.1.3 gives the modular channel list
    and the order jpxl-decode returns its planes in. Readable with
    jpxl_conformance::FloatImage::from_npy.
    Regenerable at any time from the fixture with the pinned djxl build.
